notes: All assigned fields examined together against supplied text and rendered PDF pp. 4–6. No target assigned using row order or numeric matching. Candidate IES-I tests: mixed memory-reporting sample n = 52, beta = -.06, t = -.55, p > .05 (p. 541); untreated mixed memory-reporting sample n = 33, beta = .35, t = 2.44, p < .05 (p. 542). Neither is restricted to current depression. Amount could also refer to IMI frequency measures rather than IES-I. The Discussion says IES-I assesses a range of intrusive responses, including emotions, thoughts and images; its predictive value cannot be attributed specifically to memory frequency (p. 543). Footnote 1 (p. 539) explicitly identifies never-depressed, recovered, and clinically depressed groups. Current depression cannot be equated with untreated status. No effect conversion or N derivation performed. Candidate beta symbols and p inequalities confirmed visually; canonical text renders beta as b and some mathematical symbols as control characters. All unassigned fields are placeholders.
